resources.name: Crucial Music
resources.description: Non-exclusive sync agency with personalized service. 50/50 sync fee split; you keep 100% writer royalties. Must own masters and publishing, have original songs, and be registered with a PRO. Three-year contract with non-exclusive rights to pitch and license; auto-renews if not canceled.

resources.name: Bodega Sync
resources.description: Division of Symphonic Distribution. Curated roster of indie artists/labels. Pre-cleared catalog for one-stop licensing. Important: must be a Symphonic client to apply; Bodega is not a standalone service for all artists. Highly selective due to competitive nature of sync licensing.

resources.name: TAXI
resources.description: Established in 1992. Publishes screened music-wanted listings from supervisors, labels, ad agencies, and game companies. Screeners review and forward qualifying tracks. Note: ~$300/year + $5/submission with reported placement rates around 6%; valuable mostly for feedback rather than placements.

resources.name: Musicbed
resources.description: Premium placements with brands like Nike, Google, Netflix, Spotify. High-quality curated catalog for film and advertising. Represents 1,500+ hand-picked artists and composers. Less than 1% acceptance rate.

resources.name: Marmoset
resources.description: Indie-focused, creative approach. Non-exclusive deals, typically 50/50 split with personalized pitching to premium clients. Has paid artists over $44M all-time. Important: submissions open in limited rolling windows only, not year-round. Watch their submissions page for open periods.
highlights: Submissions open in limited windows only

resources.name: Audio Network
resources.description: One of the largest global sync libraries with 300,000+ tracks. Transparent pricing, broadcast-ready music. International roster. Artists fill out submission form with links/files; A&R team reviews and responds if music fits their style and quality standards.
highlights: Note: response rates can be low due to volume

resources.name: Jingle Punks
resources.description: Award-winning agency with offices in NYC, LA, Toronto, London. 400,000+ song library, 4,000+ artists. Exclusive contracts, 50/50 split on sync license fees. Requires all submissions be fully mixed and mastered—no demos, works in progress, or cover songs.

resources.name: Nightingale Music
resources.description: The main production music library was acquired by EMI Production Music (April 2020) and is now owned by SONY/KPM. In US/Canada, contact APM Music; worldwide, contact KPM Music. However, the Nightingale Indie Label remains independently managed at nightingalemusic.com and does accept submissions for artist-driven sync content.

resources.name: Pond5
resources.description: One of the largest royalty-free media marketplaces (25M+ stock clips). Part of Shutterstock family. Artists upload tracks and set their own prices. Important pricing change (Jan 15, 2025): non-exclusive artists now earn 30% royalty per sale; exclusive video artists earn 40%. No upfront costs to upload.
resources.cost: Free to upload; 30% artist royalty (non-exclusive) or 40% (exclusive video)

resources.name: Artlist
resources.description: Subscription model for buyers. Curated catalog with high production standards. Popular with content creators and filmmakers. Music submissions are currently closed. Accepting submissions for SFX, filmmakers, motion designers, and template artists only.

resources.name: Epidemic Sound
resources.description: Artists receive upfront payments and revenue shares. 50/50 streaming royalty split forever plus access to a $4.2M annual Soundtrack Bonus pool (increased from $3.7M). Note: full buy-out contracts mean composers transfer rights and lose PRO royalties. New artist applications currently closed. Major announcement: 43% increase in artist bonus payments beginning 2026, plus $1M fund for AI-related adaptations.

resources.name: Jamendo
resources.description: Accessible platform for indie musicians. Free uploads, non-exclusive. Unlimited submissions. YouTube Content ID integration. Founded 2004 with 70,000+ musicians and 600,000+ tracks. Warning: Jamendo is pursuing legal action against Nvidia and Suno for alleged unauthorized use of its catalog to train AI models (alerted end of 2024). Artists should be aware their Jamendo-hosted content may have been exposed to AI training datasets.

resources.name: Ditto Pro (Sync Dashboard)
resources.description: Ditto Pro subscribers access sync briefs across TV, film, and ad campaigns. Ditto reviews tracks and pitches on your behalf. Sync licensing only available on Pro plan. Price is £59/year (approximately $75–77 USD at current exchange rates).
resources.cost: £59/yr (~$75–77 USD) as part of Ditto Pro
highlights: ⚠️ Price increased in USD terms vs. original $59 listing

resources.name: Sync Money
resources.description: Leading online community for sync licensing. Provides insider knowledge, industry connections, and access to real opportunities. Free newsletter sends curated sync briefs that subscribers can submit to. Website and blog last updated April 2025. Focus on getting real opportunities for music makers in TV, Film, Advertising, Video Games.

resources.name: Nitrility
resources.description: Blockchain-powered music-licensing marketplace. Search, request, negotiate, and clear sync licenses for songs from a 200-million-song catalog. Trusted by 80,000+ artists, labels, and publishers. Features include AI-powered search, expert curation, automated notifications, contract handling, payments, and dispute protection. Free to browse and sign up; license prices vary by rights-holder. Raised $500K Seed round (June 2025). Important: seller access still limited to test group; full opening to all rights-holders pending.
resources.cost: Free to browse; license prices vary

resources.name: One Night Stand Music & Management
resources.description: Subscription-based sync licensing model. Direct pitching to film, TV, ads, gaming. Artists keep ownership of music and avoid losing rights. Zero commission on placements—flat subscription fee replaces commission model. Almost all opportunities are non-exclusive. Transparent, flexible approach focused on artist control.

resources.name: Music Vine
resources.description: UK-based curated music licensing platform. High-quality curation with hand-picked approach. Each track must be reviewed and approved. Artists need at least 50% exclusive catalog with platform. Revenue split: 60% on exclusive tracks, 35% on non-exclusive. Known for quality over quantity and strong placement opportunities for independent composers. Important: AI policy (updated July 21, 2025) states they cannot accept music fully generated by AI. Artist applications currently closed.

resources.name: Millennial Mind Sync — Supervisor Directory
resources.description: 325+ music supervisors indexed with LinkedIn profiles, email contact methods, and project histories. Includes a free pitch email generator tool.

resources.name: SongwriterUniverse — Supervisors Directory
resources.description: Free list of music supervisors in the US, Canada, and UK with company names, addresses, and contact info.

resources.name: Guild of Music Supervisors
resources.description: Non-profit organization for music supervision professionals. News, events, and the GMS Awards; the member directory requires a login. Useful for researching who supervises what.
resources.cost: Free to browse; Friend of the Guild $100/yr

resources.name: Aristake — Sync Agents Guide
resources.description: Free guide listing sync agents and how to get music synced on TV, video games, and films. By Ari's Take Academy instructor Vo Williams. Reports 250+ students signed to sync agencies to date.

resources.name: Musco Sound — Library Submission Guide
resources.description: Free guide with direct links to submit music to various tiers of sync libraries. Note: this is a 2017 blog post and content may be outdated; recommend finding more current submission guides.

resources.name: IMDb / IMDb Pro
resources.description: Look up music supervisors by searching film/TV credits. IMDb Pro provides contact details and project history. Monthly plan: $19.99/month; annual plan: $149.99/year (better value at $12.50/month). Group plan available at $79.99/month for up to 5 members. Amazon Prime members save up to 60% on first year.

resources.name: The Sync Report
resources.description: Comprehensive directory of 600+ music supervisors, music buyers, and ad agency contacts in USA, UK, Canada, and Australia. TV calendar showing what films and shows are currently in development. Includes production calendars for optimal pitch timing and weekly industry updates.

resources.name: Music Business Registry — Film & TV Music Guide
resources.description: Industry-standard directory for 30+ years. Thousands of listings with direct phone/email. Covers supervisors, studios, licensing execs, game companies. Multiple format options available: PDF Edition ($150), Print Edition ($325), Print + PDF combo ($750), CSV File ($275).
resources.cost: From $150 (PDF edition); Print, CSV, and bundle options available

resources.name: Underground Mix — Sync Library Submission List
resources.description: 120+ vetted sync libraries, micro-licensing sites, and music houses. Includes submission checklist and email pitch template. Created by former Extreme Music / Paramount / Sony professionals. Annual URL update (previously /library2025, now /library2026).

resources.name: Music Supervisors Directory
resources.description: Redirects to The Sync Report. Curated directory of 600+ music supervisor contacts in LA, NYC, London, Canada, and Australia. Updated monthly. Subscription-based access.

resources.name: Songtrust — Sync Crash Course
resources.description: Free crash course covering sync licensing fundamentals: deal structures, sync fees, rights, placement types, and royalty collection. Songtrust is a leading publishing administration platform.

resources.name: The Sync Lab (Aaron Davison)
resources.description: Free 4-hour video course covering how to create sync-ready music, pitch effectively, and land placements. Includes a free licensing directory.

resources.name: Dark Horse Institute — Sync Guide
resources.description: Blog with strategies and tips for getting sync placements as an independent musician. Dark Horse Institute is a music school in Nashville.

resources.name: Collabhouse — Demystifying Sync Licensing
resources.description: Guide explaining how sync licensing works as a revenue stream and exposure tool for independent artists. Note: URL is on a 'legacy' subdomain, suggesting content may have been migrated or archived; recommend checking if main collabhouse.com is still active.

resources.name: 2Indie — The Sync Society
resources.description: Private music licensing club. Weekly Zoom calls with industry professionals (sync agencies, supervisors, producers). Monthly curated sync sampler sent to agencies. 14-day money-back guarantee.

resources.name: Elite Music Coaching (Michael Elsner & Jody Friedman)
resources.description: Sync licensing training from producer Michael Elsner (3,000+ placements) and music supervisor Jody Friedman, formerly Master Music Licensing. Programs include the Sync Placement Academy course and the Sync Titan private members' community.

resources.name: Ari's Take Academy — Advanced Sync Strategies
resources.description: Step-by-step course on sync licensing including how to get signed to agents. Includes showcases with top-tier sync agencies and direct submission opportunities. Enrollment opens and closes in cohorts. One-time payment of $997, or flexible monthly payment (~$62/month via Klarna/Afterpay).

resources.name: Sync My Music
resources.description: Free sync licensing course for producers covering creating licensable music, finding libraries, and building income through performance royalties. Paid memberships (Sync Academy, Sync Edge) add production tutorials and library recommendations.

resources.name: ThatPitch Blog
resources.description: Extensive articles on sync licensing opportunities, companies, fees, strategies, and trends. Very active platform with multiple sync licensing articles and guides published through 2025.

resources.name: Millennial Mind Sync Blog
resources.description: Articles on sync libraries, music supervisors, submission strategies, and free tools (music supervisor pitch generator, beat pricing calculator). Last updated February 2024.

resources.name: Stock Music Musician
resources.description: Blog focused on production music and sync library submissions with reviews and guides.

resources.name: The Sync Report Podcast
resources.description: Podcast connecting songwriters with the sync licensing industry. Last new episode published February 2023; 47-episode archive remains available.

resources.name: Rareform Audio Blog
resources.description: Articles on how sync licensing empowers independent artists outside traditional label structures.
